title.en: Who Are You at the Board-Game Table?
title.zh: 桌游一桌人：你会带来哪种玩法？

description.en: Six casual game-night choices about learning rules, enjoying a challenge and helping mixed experience levels play together. Find your table portrait.
description.zh: 六次休闲桌游选择，学习规则、享受挑战、让经验不同的人同桌玩，发现你在这一桌的趣味画像。

introduction.en: Think of a friendly board game with no money at stake. Choose what you would enjoy doing when the table includes both familiar and new players. The result describes this game-night scene, not intelligence, leadership or your worth as a friend.
introduction.zh: 想象一场不涉及金钱的友好桌游，同桌既有熟手也有新手。选你会喜欢怎样参与。结果只描述这场游戏，不评智力、领导力或朋友价值。

focus.en: Making rules understandable, pursuing an interesting challenge and keeping a mixed-experience table enjoyable.
focus.zh: 让规则易懂、追求有趣挑战，以及让经验不同的一桌人继续享受游戏。

prompt.en: A new game is opened. You would like to…

label.en: Walk through one example turn before starting.
label.zh: 开始前演示一个示例回合。

label.en: Look for a move that might create an interesting contest.
label.zh: 看看什么走法会带来有趣较量。

label.en: Ask how much explanation and practice the group wants.
label.zh: 问大家想听多少说明、练多久。

prompt.en: A rule is unclear during the first round. You…
prompt.zh: 第一轮碰到不清楚的规则，你会……

label.en: Check the relevant line and agree how to use it this round.
label.zh: 核对相关一条，约好本轮怎样用。

label.en: Suggest a quick shared ruling so the contest can continue.
label.zh: 提议快速达成共同判法，让较量继续。

label.en: Check that the new player understands before moving on.
label.zh: 确认新玩家明白了再继续。

prompt.en: One player has a strong early lead. You find yourself…
prompt.zh: 一名玩家早早领先，你发现自己……

label.en: Enjoying the puzzle of how another player could catch up.
label.zh: 享受其他人如何追上的走法难题。

label.en: Pointing out a rule interaction that anyone can use.
label.zh: 指出任何人都可使用的规则关联。

label.en: Checking whether everyone still wants the same kind of round.
label.zh: 问大家是否仍想玩同样的这一轮。

prompt.en: A beginner asks for advice on their turn. You…
prompt.zh: 新手在自己回合求建议，你会……

label.en: Ask whether they want a hint or just time to try.
label.zh: 问想要提示，还是只想多点时间试。

label.en: Show two legal options without choosing for them.
label.zh: 说明两种合法选项，不替对方选。

label.en: Describe the interesting tradeoff between two competitive moves.
label.zh: 讲两种竞争性走法之间有趣的取舍。

prompt.en: The table has time for one more game. You suggest…
prompt.zh: 还有时间再玩一局，你提议……

label.en: A round with a fresh strategic constraint everyone accepts.
label.zh: 一轮大家都接受的新策略限制。

label.en: A quick recap of the rules that caused confusion.
label.zh: 简短回顾刚才引起困惑的规则。

label.en: Asking whether the group wants a rematch, a lighter game or a finish.
label.zh: 问大家想重赛、轻松换局，还是结束。

prompt.en: What would make this game night feel successful?
prompt.zh: 什么会让这场桌游夜让你满足？

label.en: Different experience levels could participate without pretending.
label.zh: 经验不同的人都能参与，不必装懂。

label.en: The group understood the game well enough to make its own choices.
label.zh: 大家懂到足以自己做选择。

label.en: There was a close or surprising contest worth talking about.
label.zh: 出现过值得聊的接近或意外较量。

summary.en: Your table portrait makes the rules usable through a concrete example. You prefer people to understand their options rather than simply copy the most experienced player. The result concerns this game scene, not a general teaching ability score.
summary.zh: 你的同桌画像通过具体示例让规则可用。你更愿大家理解选项，而非照抄最熟练的人。结果只谈这场游戏，不给通用教学能力打分。

example.en: You might demonstrate drawing a card, choosing an action and ending a turn with spare pieces before asking a new player to make their first real move.
example.zh: 你可能用备用棋子演示抽牌、选动作、结束回合，再让新手做第一步正式走法。

strength.en: One example can make an abstract rule easier to follow and help a newcomer ask a question they could not form from the rulebook alone.
strength.zh: 一个示例能让抽象规则易跟随，也帮新人问出只读规则书时还说不清的问题。

tradeoff.en: Explaining too far ahead can become another barrier. A short usable example may serve the table better than showing every possible exception at once.
tradeoff.zh: 解释太超前也会成障碍。简短可用示例，可能比一次展示所有例外更适合这一桌。

experiment.en: When explaining one recreational rule, show one ordinary turn and stop for a question. Add the next detail only when the group needs it.
experiment.zh: 解释一条休闲规则时，演示一个普通回合就停下等提问。到大家需要时再添下一细节。

summary.en: You enjoy a table where moves create an interesting contest. A comeback, a constraint or a surprising interaction gives you something to explore. The portrait does not equate winning with value, and a close contest can be satisfying regardless of the final score.
summary.zh: 你喜欢走法能形成有趣较量的一桌。追赶、限制或意外关联，让你有可探索之处。画像不把获胜等同价值，比分接近的过程也可以与最终胜负无关地满足。

example.en: You might enjoy testing an unfamiliar opening in a rematch because it changes the contest, even if it gives you a less certain chance of winning.
example.zh: 重赛时，你可能愿试陌生开局，因为它改变了较量，即使自己赢的把握更小。

strength.en: An interesting challenge can keep a familiar game lively and provide a concrete focus for talking about choices after the round.
strength.zh: 有趣挑战能让熟悉游戏保持活力，也给赛后讨论选择一个具体焦点。

tradeoff.en: A challenge that delights you may overwhelm someone learning the basics. Agreeing on the level of competition keeps the contest shared rather than imposed.
tradeoff.zh: 让你兴奋的挑战，可能压住正在学基础的人。约好竞争程度，较量才是共同选择而非强加。

experiment.en: Before a rematch, ask whether everyone wants a competitive round or a practice round. Enjoy the chosen version without treating either as lesser.
experiment.zh: 重赛前，问大家想认真较量还是练习。享受共同选中的版本，不把哪种看得更低。

title.zh: 不同经验同桌的照应者

summary.en: Your game night makes room for people who need different amounts of help, time or intensity. You ask what kind of round the table wants. This ending values a shared fit without making you responsible for everybody’s mood.
summary.zh: 你的桌游夜给需要不同帮助、时间或强度的人留空间。你会问这一桌想玩怎样的一轮。结局珍惜共同合适，不让你对每个人心情负责。

example.en: When a beginner pauses, you might ask whether they want a hint, more thinking time or a simpler practice round rather than assuming which would help.
example.zh: 新手停住时，你可能问想要提示、多想一会儿还是简单练习，不替对方假定哪种有帮助。

strength.en: A direct check-in can keep differences in experience from becoming embarrassment and allow people to take part on terms they understand.
strength.zh: 直接询问能让经验差异少变成尴尬，也让人按自己明白的条件参与。

tradeoff.en: Checking every moment can interrupt the game. An agreed signal for help or a break may let the group relax without constant monitoring.
tradeoff.zh: 时刻询问也会打断游戏。约一个求助或休息信号，可能让大家不用持续监测也能放松。

experiment.en: At one casual group activity, ask once how people want help offered. Agree on a simple signal and then enjoy participating yourself.
experiment.zh: 一次休闲群体活动里，问一次大家希望怎样获得帮助。约简单信号后，也让自己享受参与。
